name: Museum of Applied Arts Frankfurt
key_features: White panelled blocks take their grid from the old Villa Metzler, linked by ramps along the Main.

name: Munkegaard School
key_features: Single-storey classrooms, each with its own small garden courtyard, laid out on a chequerboard grid.

name: Wittgenstein House
key_features: Austere plastered cubes with tall steel doors and windows, every proportion refined by Wittgenstein.

name: Hôtel Guimard
key_features: Guimard's own house on a triangular plot, with oval rooms and a flowing, carved-stone facade.

name: Steinhaus
key_features: Shards of concrete, steel and glass break out of a lakeside slope, a built autobiography of rock and fissure.

name: The Atheneum
key_features: White panelled visitor centre where a ramp winds up through grids skewed to the town and the river.

name: Liederhalle
key_features: Concert halls with free, non-rectangular plans, the walls faced in mosaics of mixed stone and glass.

name: Utzon House, Hellebæk
key_features: Long low house: a solid brick north wall and a fully glazed south side open to the beech forest.

name: MUSE Science Museum
key_features: Sharp sloping roofs echo the mountains; a tall central void hangs animal specimens in mid-air.

name: National Building Museum
key_features: Brick hall ringed by a sculpted frieze; giant Corinthian columns rise through its vast atrium.

name: Tribunal de Paris
key_features: Glass courthouse of three stacked, stepped blocks with planted terraces above a vast public hall.

name: Weltstadthaus Peek & Cloppenburg
key_features: A curved glass shell held on laminated timber ribs wraps a department store along the street.

name: Hagen Crematorium
key_features: Temple-like crematorium faced in black and white marble geometry, after Florentine Romanesque.

name: Thomas Jefferson Building, Library of Congress
key_features: A Beaux-Arts dome rises over an octagonal reading room ringed by alcoves, beyond a marble great hall.

name: Istituto Marchiondi Spagliardi
key_features: A boys' reformatory with a raw concrete frame, stairs and walkways left bare and fully expressed.

name: Notre-Dame de Royan
key_features: Thin V-section concrete shells rise in a crown of fins, with tall coloured glass between them.

name: Musiktheater im Revier
key_features: A fully glazed foyer facade puts Yves Klein's vast blue sponge reliefs on show to the street.

name: Großmarkthalle
key_features: A long row of thin concrete shell barrel vaults spans the market hall between two end blocks.

name: Haus der Kulturen der Welt (Kongresshalle)
key_features: A saddle-shaped roof sweeps up between two outer arches over an auditorium set on a broad podium.

name: Nemausus
key_features: Two ship-like aluminium-clad slabs on pilotis with open access galleries and generous double-height flats.

name: Rufer House
key_features: A near-cubic plain block whose freely placed windows follow an early Raumplan of split-level rooms.

name: Retti Candle Shop
key_features: A tiny shop front of polished aluminium with a narrow keyhole-like door and mirrors that enlarge the interior.

name: Hans Otto Theater
key_features: Three red curved shell roofs cantilever over a glazed foyer and auditorium on the shore of a lake.

name: El Capricho
key_features: Brick villa banded with green sunflower tiles, entered under a slender minaret-like tower on stone columns.

name: Siedlung Halen
key_features: Dense terraced row houses of exposed concrete step down a wooded slope around a shared village square.

name: Messner Mountain Museum Corones
key_features: Museum buried in a mountain summit, with only curving concrete canopies and a jutting viewing window showing.

name: Maison Blanche
key_features: The young Jeanneret's white rendered villa for his parents, a compact block set into a sloping garden.

name: Green Building (MIT Building 54)
key_features: A slab-like concrete research tower with a gridded window wall, raised over an open, windy ground floor.

name: The Gateway
key_features: Two trapezoid-plan glass towers read as thin flat blades from some angles, framing a gateway.

name: Society Hill Towers
key_features: Three concrete-grid apartment towers with deep-set windows stand above rows of low townhouses.

name: Holyoke Center (Smith Campus Center)
key_features: A long concrete slab with a public arcade cut through its base between two streets.

name: Palmolive Building
key_features: A limestone Art Deco tower of stepped setbacks rising to a beacon mast.

name: Villa Fallet
by: Charles-Édouard Jeanneret (Le Corbusier) with René Chapallaz
key_features: Jeanneret's first house: a steep chalet roof and sgraffito facades with fir-tree motifs.

name: Großes Festspielhaus
key_features: A wide festival hall cut partly into the Mönchsberg rock sits behind the old court-stables facade.

name: Fisher Center for the Performing Arts
key_features: Billowing stainless-steel canopies drape over a plain theatre box and sweep out over the entrance.

name: Westmount Square
key_features: Dark steel-and-glass towers and a low glass pavilion stand on a plaza above an underground mall.

name: Tancredo Neves Pantheon of the Fatherland
key_features: A dove-like white form of curved wings floats over a memorial hall on the Three Powers Plaza.

name: Villa Esche
key_features: A calm villa whose rooms, furniture and fittings van de Velde designed as one flowing whole.

name: Perret Tower
key_features: One of the first reinforced-concrete towers: a slender shaft of openwork concrete built for an exhibition.

name: Glaspalast Sindelfingen
key_features: Glass-walled steel hall whose transparent skin opens the sports and events floor to the town.

name: Muziekcentrum Vredenburg
key_features: Concert hall with the audience on all sides, set in a structuralist frame of repeated concrete units.

name: Skagen Odde Nature Centre
key_features: Clustered white halls with tall roof lanterns sit low among the dunes.

name: Lisbon Port Control Tower
key_features: A leaning dark prism at the mouth of the Tagus, with the glazed control room at its tilted top.

name: Gosstrakh Apartments
key_features: Early Constructivist flats: a plain block with long window bands and corner balconies, a step to Narkomfin.

name: Langer Eugen
key_features: Slim office tower wrapped in Eiermann's outer layer of walkways and sunshades.

name: PPG Place
key_features: Mirror-glass towers bristling with Gothic-style spires and pinnacles around a public plaza.

name: Okanoyama Museum of Art
key_features: Tile-clad gallery boxes set in a straight line like train carriages beside the railway.

name: Garage with Chauffeur's Flat
key_features: A steel frame with bolted precast concrete panels: an early test of prefabricated building.

name: Hallfield Primary School
key_features: Classrooms are clustered like petals along a curving corridor, freeing the plan from a rigid grid.

name: Joieria Roca
key_features: A rationalist jewellery shop whose glazed shopfront and white walls turn a Passeig de Gràcia corner.

name: Jardinette Apartments
key_features: Neutra's first American building: a concrete frame wrapped in continuous horizontal bands of windows.

name: Märkisches Museum
key_features: A brick collage of Brandenburg Gothic and Renaissance quotes, with a tower modelled on a medieval keep.

name: Kollhoff Tower
key_features: A dark brick tower with a sharp wedge corner and setbacks, recalling 1920s American skyscrapers.

name: James A. Farley Building (Moynihan Train Hall)
key_features: A Corinthian colonnade fronts the old mail hall, now a skylit train hall under its exposed steel trusses.

name: Kulturpalast Dresden
key_features: A long glass-walled hall under a broad flat roof, with a socialist-realist mural across one end.

name: Stadsschouwburg Utrecht
key_features: A brick theatre of stacked cubic volumes with a tall fly tower and long horizontal lines.

name: National Space Centre
key_features: A semi-transparent tower of ETFE cushions holds upright rockets beside the low museum hall.

name: Place Bonaventure
key_features: A ribbed-concrete megastructure stacks exhibition halls, offices and a rooftop hotel over rail tracks.

name: The Lowry
key_features: An arts centre of colliding metal-clad volumes on a waterfront point, with brightly coloured interiors.

name: Glasgow School of Art
key_features: Huge north-light studio windows on a stone front, with tall oriel windows lighting the west wing library.

name: Pampulha Art Museum (former Casino)
key_features: A glass-walled former casino on Pampulha lake, with ramps inside and a curving dance-hall wing.

name: Institute of Contemporary Art, Boston
key_features: Galleries cantilever over the harbourwalk, with timber bleacher steps and a mediatheque tilted to the water.

name: Everson Museum of Art
key_features: Cantilevered bush-hammered concrete gallery boxes pinwheel around a central sculpture court.

name: Geschwister-Scholl-Schule
key_features: Classrooms grouped as separate 'class homes', each with its own small garden court, off a winding hall.

name: Palazzo Piccolomini
key_features: Rusticated palazzo modelled on Palazzo Rucellai, with tiered loggias opening its garden to the valley.

name: Museum of Military History (Arsenal)
key_features: Banded brick facades in a Byzantine-Moorish style front a domed hall of fame inside Vienna's Arsenal.

name: Palazzo dell'Arte (Triennale di Milano)
key_features: Muzio's brick exhibition palace in Parco Sempione, entered through tall arches to a grand central stair.

name: Opus Hong Kong
key_features: Glass-walled floors of flats shift and twist as the tower rises up a steep hillside on the Peak.

name: Tagblatt-Turm
key_features: An early exposed-concrete high-rise whose tower steps back above a lower block.

name: UTEC University Campus
key_features: A stepped concrete 'man-made cliff' of terraces and open-air platforms facing a ravine and the city.

name: La Congiunta
key_features: Windowless concrete gallery of linked rooms lit only from above, housing bronze sculptures.

name: Supreme Federal Court
key_features: A glass box under a flat roof slab, carried on slender sculpted columns facing the Three Powers Plaza.

name: Palmach Museum
key_features: Galleries sink into a dune behind layered walls of local sandstone, built around the site's existing trees.

name: Museo Jumex
key_features: Travertine-clad block raised on columns, with a sawtooth roof bringing north light into the top galleries.

name: Palacio Barolo
key_features: Office tower laid out after Dante's Divine Comedy, from a vaulted ground arcade to a lighthouse crown.

name: Rockefeller Museum
key_features: White limestone galleries around a cloister court with a long pool, marked by an octagonal tower.

name: Memorial to the Deportees, Yad Vashem
key_features: An original deportation cattle car stands at the end of a broken rail track cantilevered over a valley.

name: Yad Kennedy
key_features: A ring of tall concrete fins shaped like a felled tree trunk encloses an eternal flame on a hilltop.

name: Teatro Regional del Biobío
key_features: Box of steel frames wrapped in translucent PTFE fabric that glows like a lantern at night.

name: Pousada de Santa Marinha
key_features: Monastery turned hotel, with a new granite wing of rooms added beside the old cloister.

name: Future University Hakodate
key_features: Huge glass hall of stepped studio terraces under one roof, built from precast concrete frames.

name: L'Arbre Blanc
by: Sou Fujimoto, Nicolas Laisné, Manal Rachdi
key_features: White tower bristling with long cantilevered balconies and sunshades like branches.

name: House of Music Hungary
key_features: Glass hall under a thin roof pierced by holes for trees, with a leaf-patterned golden ceiling.

name: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel Stadium
key_features: Folded-plate concrete roof cantilevered over the stands, the structure left fully on show.

name: Pakistan Monument
key_features: Four large and three small granite petals open in a ring, their inner faces carved with murals.

name: Independence Memorial Hall
key_features: Open pillared hall under a tiered Kandyan roof, modelled on a royal audience hall.

name: School of the Arts, Singapore
key_features: Teaching blocks above a public podium of theatres, with green walls and shaded breezeways.

name: People's Park Complex
key_features: Shopping podium with a central atrium 'city room' below a long slab block of flats.

name: Singapore Conference Hall
key_features: Glazed hall under a broad overhanging roof, with sunshading fins along its facades.

name: National Monument (Indonesia)
key_features: Tall obelisk tipped with a gilded flame, rising from a square platform in Merdeka Square.

name: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
key_features: Grey granite block on a stepped base with a portico of square columns, facing Ba Dinh Square.

name: Hanoi Museum
key_features: Inverted stepped pyramid, each floor wider than the one below, around a spiralling ramp.

name: National Stadium, Singapore
key_features: Thin steel dome spanning the whole bowl, with a retractable roof that slides shut for shade.

name: National Theatre, Lagos
key_features: Saddle-shaped concrete hall with a folded rim, often likened to a general's cap, on an open site.

name: Voortrekker Monument
key_features: Granite block whose dome oculus sends a single sunbeam onto the cenotaph once a year.

name: Unknown Soldier Memorial, Cairo
key_features: Hollow pyramid of four separate concrete walls leaning together over the tomb of the unknown soldier.

name: Odunpazarı Modern Museum
key_features: Stacked timber boxes echoing the Ottoman houses around it, around a skylit central atrium.

name: Negev Brigade Monument
key_features: Concrete sculptural landscape of a tower, dome, tunnel and water channel in the desert.

name: Museo Universitario Arte Contemporáneo
key_features: Long sloping glass facade under a concrete roof, opening the galleries to a plaza.

name: Torre Reforma
key_features: Two exposed-concrete walls carry the tower; a diagonal steel frame holds the glass sides.
